newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.

text.p: Shorter Swedish debt yields rose in line with Finnish ones after Finland's central bank said on Monday it would consider tighter monetary policy if inflation accelerated more.
"We have had a spillover effect from Finland where short debt yields rose," one dealer said.
The Finnish central bank said risks for accelerating inflation had risen, raising fears of an interest rate rise.
T-bill rates fell some basis points.
"Nothing in particular has happened. We have seen some interest in placing liquidity," one dealer said.
News on the agreement regarding the European stability pact did not affect the Swedish market, dealers said.
Market focus remains on the EU summit in Amsterdam and U.S. data -- CPI, housing starts, industrial production and capacity utilisation which are due on Tuesday.

The six month T-bill rate fell three basis points to 4.14 percent and ten year bond yield was unchanged at 6.77 percent. The crown was steady at 4.4780 crowns to the mark versus 4.4770 crowns late on Friday.
